Why the committee made the rec ommendations

The committee agreed the risk factors for fragility fractures included in the 2012 NICE

guideline on osteoporosis were still relevant to current practice and agreed to keep

these in the rec ommendations.

The committee agreed that all people aged 50 and over and women who have

experienced menopause are most at risk of fragility fractures.

There was also

evidence to support doing a risk assessment if they have had a previous fragility

fracture or they are currently using, or frequently use, systemic glu cocorticoids.

The committee agreed that there is likely to be significantly higher risk of further

fragility fracture in people who have previously had one.

They also noted fracture

a fragility fracture with the aim of reducing further fractures.

Why is this recommendation and topic important?

Osteoporotic fractures are associated with psychological distress, subsequent fractures, loss of independence, reduced ability to perform activities of daily living, and death.

Evidence shows that only 40% to 60% of persons experiencing a hip fracture recover their prefracture level of mobility and ability to perform activities of daily living.

The age-adjusted prevalence of osteoporosis is 12.6% among community dwelling US residents 50 years or older.
